subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
title: Homologous Series
summary: Methane, ethane, propane, butane: four different compounds, one family. How each member differs from the next by one CH₂ unit, and what that means for their properties.
keyPoints: A **homologous series** is a series of organic compounds with the **same functional group** and the **same general formula**, in which successive members differ by **–CH₂–**.
Each member is a **homologue**. Successive members differ in molar mass by **14 u** (CH₂ = 12 + 2).
Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: CH₄ → C₂H₆ → C₃H₈ → C₄H₁₀ → C₅H₁₂, each one CH₂ more.
**Chemical properties are similar** (not identical), because the members share the same functional group.
**Physical properties change gradually** with chain length: boiling point rises, for example.

blocks.p: All of them burn in oxygen to give CO₂ and H₂O, and all undergo substitution with chlorine in light: similar chemistry. The boiling point rises steadily as the chain grows, because larger molecules attract one another more strongly. Boiling points at 1 atm (CRC Handbook).

quiz.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by:
The molar mass difference between successive homologues is:
Which is the next member after C₃H₈ in the alkane series?
quiz.explain: Add CH₂: C₃H₈ + CH₂ = C₄H₁₀, which fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

quiz.q: Members of a homologous series have:
quiz.explain: Similar, not identical: the same functional group; physical properties change gradually.

quiz.q: Which pair belongs to the same homologous series?
quiz.explain: Both are alcohols and differ by one CH₂.

simulation.reason: Predicting the next member is a test students can run on families the reel never shows (alcohols and carboxylic acids), and the pair test makes them apply all three conditions, including spotting that CH₄ and C₂H₄ or C₂H₆ and C₂H₅OH are not homologues, which the reel can only state.
simulation.objective: Predict each next member of a series, see the +CH₂, +14 u pattern and the rising boiling point, and decide whether two compounds are homologues.
instructions: Choose a family: alkanes, alcohols or carboxylic acids.
Predict the formula of the next member.
Add CH₂ and check your prediction.
Read the table: formula, molar mass and boiling point.
In part 4, decide whether each pair is in the same series.
